n: Everest Base Camp via Gokyo & Cho La
sum: A 16-day loop from Lukla up the Gokyo valley, over the 5,420 m Cho La to Lobuche, on to Everest Base Camp and Kala Patthar, and back down the main trail.

guide.note: Khumbu has not enforced the national guide requirement, so the route can be walked independently. The Ngozumpa Glacier crossing and the Cho La are the reason to hire a licensed guide here: neither has a fixed trail, the safe line changes each season, and a guide will also judge whether the pass should be attempted at all on the day.

access: You fly to Lukla to start and from Lukla to finish. Departures are in the first hours of the morning, from Kathmandu or, in peak season, from Manthali in Ramechhap, and they depend entirely on the weather at the Lukla end. Allow for a day's delay in either direction.

photo.a: Four trekkers follow a trodden track across a broad snowfield on the Cho La, with rock peaks streaked with snow and scattered clouds behind.
photo.c: Crossing the glacier on the Cho La

includes: porter in most packages (the cheapest tiers leave one out)
Sagarmatha park and Khumbu municipality permits
lodge beds and three meals a day on the trek
airport transfers; Kathmandu hotel nights in some packages

permits.name: Sagarmatha National Park entry permit
permits.where: At the park gate in Monjo, or in advance at the park counter in the Tourist Service Centre, Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu.

permits.name: Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality entry permit
permits.where: At the municipality's tourist information centre in Lukla when you land, or at the Monjo checkpoint if you walk in from the road. It cannot be bought in Kathmandu.

transportText: Flights to Lukla and back, from Kathmandu or (in the busy months) from Manthali with a night drive to the airstrip
tips: Carry microspikes and poles for the pass, and keep one spare day to sit out bad weather at Thagnak if the Cho La is not in condition.
At Gokyo and Thagnak, ask who crossed the pass that day and how long they took. Lodge owners know more than any forecast.
Dzongla has only a few lodges. In peak season have your guide phone ahead from Thagnak, or leave early enough to arrive by early afternoon.
If you hire a porter, check that they have boots, sunglasses and a warm jacket for the pass. As their employer, that is your job.
Bring cash for the whole route from Kathmandu or Namche; nothing higher up dispenses money.

days.t: Fly to Lukla, walk to Phakding
days.note: A short, mostly downhill introduction after the flight: through Chheplung and Ghat to the lodges beside the river at Phakding. Drink plenty and go to bed early.

The trail crosses the Dudh Koshi several times and passes the permit check at Monjo. The 600 m climb beyond the last bridge is the first real test. Pause at the rest point halfway, where Everest shows through the trees on a clear day.
med: Um Hong Gil Namche Community Hospital

days.note: Climb to the Everest View Hotel at 3,880 m, look up the valley toward Tengboche and Everest, the way you will come home at the end of the trek, and return to Namche to sleep. Buy anything you have forgotten; the real shops stop here.
med: Um Hong Gil Namche Community Hospital

days.note: Turn off the main trail at Sanasa and climb to Mong La at 3,973 m, drop steeply to the river at Phortse Tenga and climb through forest to Dole. You gain 600 m of sleeping height today, so keep the pace gentle from the start.

Three hours across open slopes above the tree line, through the summer pastures of Lhafarma and Luza. Kangtega and Thamserku stand behind you and Cho Oyu ahead. Spend the afternoon resting, not exploring.

A second night at the same height before the lakes. Stroll up the ridge behind the lodges in the morning, come down for lunch and drink a lot. People who skip this day often pay for it at Gokyo or on the pass.

Past Pangka the path climbs stone steps beside the glacier's outflow and passes two smaller lakes before reaching Gokyo on the third. Arrive for lunch; tomorrow's hill is in plain view across the water.
Climb Gokyo Ri, 570 m above the lake, in two to three hours. From the top you look across the glacier to the side valley that leads to the Cho La. Rest for the remainder of the day and eat well.

days.t: Across the Ngozumpa Glacier to Thagnak
days.note: A short crossing on a path over rubble and round melt ponds that moves every year; follow the newest cairns. You reach Thagnak by lunch. Pack tonight, fill your bottles and order an early breakfast.

Leave by five. Two hours up a valley to a ridge, a short drop into a basin of boulders, then a steep scramble on loose rock to the pass. On the far side walk down the snow of the glacier on the trodden line, then down rock slabs and a grassy valley to Dzongla.

An easy half day. The trail contours above Chola Tsho with Ama Dablam framed down the valley, rounds a spur into the Khumbu valley and joins the main base camp trail for the last stretch to Lobuche. Rest in the afternoon.

days.t: Lobuche to Gorak Shep and Everest Base Camp
days.note: Along the moraine to Gorak Shep for an early lunch, then out over glacier rubble to base camp and back. It is a long, slow day above 5,000 m. Fix a turnaround time before you leave and stick to it.

days.t: Kala Patthar, then down to Pheriche
days.note: Up Kala Patthar by headlamp for the dawn view, about 400 m above Gorak Shep, back for breakfast, then steadily down past Lobuche and Thukla to Pheriche. You sleep more than 900 m lower and feel the difference.
A long descent with two climbs in it: up to the monastery at Tengboche and up again from the river at Phunki Tenga. Trees, warmth and thicker air come back through the day.
med: Um Hong Gil Namche Community Hospital

days.note: Down the Namche hill to the river and along the valley, finishing with the climb into Lukla. Reconfirm your flight at the airline office when you get in.
A morning flight to Kathmandu or Manthali if the sky is clear. When it is not, the choices are to wait, to share a helicopter or to walk out toward the road at Thamdanda.
